characters.description: Fortune's Folly's dimensional mage and a co-arbiter of Closetland. An outside influence is affecting his judgment, so he accepts Etja's authority over the party's dealings while the group considers a Littan expedition.
characters.name: Arlo Xor'Drel

characters.description: Arlo's soul-linked Delve co-operator and partner in developing Closetland. Unlike most of Fortune's Folly, he appears unaffected by the influence altering the party's decisions and relays Etja's approvals to the others.
characters.name: Grotto

characters.description: Fortune's Folly's frontline swordsman. His unusual conduct is among the early signs that an outside force is changing the party's priorities and judgment, leaving him subject to Etja's authority during outside dealings.
characters.name: Varrin

characters.description: A divine fighter and healer in Fortune's Folly. She is affected by the same hidden influence as most of the party, but continues with the group under Etja's safeguards while they cautiously pursue diplomacy and advancement.
characters.name: Xim

characters.description: A construct-bodied mage whose mental defenses resist much of the party's unknown influence. The group gives her final authority over outside dealings while its members cannot trust their own decisions.
characters.name: Etja

characters.description: Fortune's Folly's alchemist, archer, and scout. The same hidden influence affecting most of the party has altered her judgment while the group considers joining a future Littan expedition.
characters.name: Nuralie

characters.description: A transactional, avatar-linked power who supplies Closetland with thousands of useful essences and warns that most of Fortune's Folly is under an influence whose explanation the affected members cannot retain.
characters.name: Avarice

characters.description: An Imperial officer who rewards Fortune's Folly after an infiltrator is exposed. He helps propose a future joint expedition pairing the party with a five-person Littan team and serves as a principal contact for the arrangement.
characters.name: Littan major

characters.description: A spectral vault guardian formed from several souls in a mechanical shell. Bound to serve the hostile Delve Core, the guardian rejects combat, prefers crafting, and accepts Arlo's plan to compromise the binding rituals and carry it to freedom.
characters.name: Spectral vault guardian

characters.description: A masked Grade 51 commander who emerges when the party damages a containment weave. He is far more powerful than the undead officers already encountered, and the remaining army submits to him immediately.
characters.name: Elder Lich general

characters.description: The defeated Core of a hostile ancient military Delve. After the undead army departs and the Delve is cleared, Arlo takes the Core into his custody. It accepts the name Throne and enters the party's care.
characters.name: Throne

characters.description: The higher power associated with Heavenly Gates, a proposed evolution that would make Arlo's portals and teleports deific while changing the Delves available to him. The party delays its decision while weighing that connection.
characters.name: Dread Star

characters.description: The power behind a fragment retained within Etja. The party begins investigating the fragment while mapping otherwise hidden anomalies in the affected members' souls.
characters.name: Hysteria

characters.description: A former enemy held as a prisoner and compelled to maintain a monster. Once a princess, she questions whether a blood-rune resurrection left her as a copy rather than the same person who died, and believes her former associates are gone.
characters.name: Captive beastmaster

characters.description: A hostile divine influence already connected to Etja's history. Nuralie's earlier work on a soul poison aimed at Orexis provides a starting point for removing a different hostile influence from the party.
characters.name: Orexis

characters.description: An Elder Lich who commands the undead Corps of Volunteers on the moon. An asylum-seeking collaborator of Avarice, the lich observes her experiments on the imprisoned Hysteria.
characters.name: Lunar Elder Lich

characters.description: A System Core operating from the moon alongside Avarice and the Corps of Volunteers.
characters.name: System Core 2

characters.description: A formidable figure controlling access to a mountain complex. The gatekeeper accepts Avarice's token for the party's admission and requires each entrant to undertake a separate test.
characters.name: Mountain gatekeeper

characters.description: A powerful young ruler encountered during Arlo's dimensional trial. She tries to expel him with spatial force, but his resistance prevents the non-consensual movement. An older ruler calls her a hatchling and says Arlo has earned her audience.
characters.name: Dimensional hatchling

characters.description: An older ruler connected to the hatchling whom Arlo encounters during his dimensional trial. She takes control of the test and returns Arlo to it by moving the rulers' chamber away from him.
characters.name: Dimensional ruler

characters.description: The Grade 25 elemental remembrance who presides over Varrin's Physical Dungeon trial. A master crafter and dangerous swordfighter, he begins a demanding sword duel with Varrin amid the dungeon's fire.
characters.name: Caldera ruler

characters.description: A massive, damaged creature, likely undead, that the System identifies only as a Great Unknown. Undead hunters bring it living victims, whose souls it extracts and consumes to restore itself.
characters.name: Great Unknown

characters.description: The silver dragon revealed when the dimensional ruler's daughter transforms during her duel with Arlo. Her durability and teleportation continue in dragon form, prompting the older ruler to end the contest.
characters.name: Dragon princess

characters.description: A colossal crystalline woman who administers Xim's divine knowledge test. She recognizes Xim as the first seeker in nearly three thousand years to pursue all seven revelations, recounts earlier failed attempts to become a divine vessel, and grants the vision that reveals the six-monolith catastrophe.
characters.name: Crystalline test administrator

characters.description: A colossal dragon and one of five rulers judging Fortune's Folly's account of Hysteria. Scarlet joins the rulers in demanding evidence after the party reports the avatar's death.
characters.name: Scarlet ruler

characters.description: One of the five dragon rulers who meet Fortune's Folly. Gold ends their magical confrontation by imposing Conciliation, temporarily preventing those affected from harming one another while the rulers assess the party's claims.
characters.name: Gold ruler

characters.description: One of the five dragon rulers who receive Fortune's Folly for an audience about Hysteria and the continuing avatar threat. Cerulean joins Scarlet, Violet, Gold, and Silver in examining the party's evidence.
characters.name: Cerulean ruler

characters.description: One of the five dragon rulers evaluating Fortune's Folly's account of Hysteria and the party's proposed information-sharing relationship. Violet joins the rulers' forceful demand for evidence about the claimed death.
characters.name: Violet ruler

characters.description: One of the five dragon rulers who receive Fortune's Folly. Silver helps assess the party's claims concerning avatars and Hysteria during an audience shaped by competing magical pressure.
characters.name: Silver ruler

characters.description: An avatar-linked power from Arlo's earlier dealings. The dragon rulers identify Fortune, along with Avarice, as an essential participant in an earlier multinational effort to build a prison for avatars with System cooperation.
characters.name: Fortune

characters.description: The level-16 officer leading the five-person Littan party assigned to travel with Fortune's Folly under the major's command. Her companion team will share the coming forest expedition while the visitors operate as foreign consultants.
characters.name: Littan captain

characters.description: An observant investigator and dimensional combat caster on the Littan companion team. He joins the expedition flight as the two parties begin assessing their new partners.
characters.name: Littan dimensional mage

characters.description: A hammer-using frontline fighter on the Littan companion team. He joins the expedition flight with the team's captain, dimensional mage, and identical-twin combatants.
characters.name: Littan frontline fighter

characters.description: The more readily perceived member of the identical-twin combatants on the Littan companion team. Her sister's concealment effect makes the contrast apparent when the teams meet.
characters.name: Littan martial twin

characters.description: One of the identical Littan twins, concealed by an effect that makes observers overlook her until Etja addresses her. Nuralie's magic keeps her perceptible to Fortune's Folly, allowing the new allies to account for her presence.
characters.name: Littan stealth-focused twin

characters.description: A huge quadrupedal mana monster directing the assault on a Littan border city. Birds that land in its living canopy emerge stronger, and five elite avian hybrids guard it while the city's automated defenses struggle against the swarm.
characters.name: Hierophant

recaps.ending: Fortune's Folly and the Littan expedition destroy the Hierophant, but only after its fallen body releases the staff that is its true surviving form. A battlefield soul rite gives Arlo an immense but temporary reserve of blessed power. With the Littan major and captain obtaining consent, Arlo and Etja teleport the entire threatened city into Closetland before the staff's next catastrophic beam lands. Arlo and the major then destroy the staff. The major players survive, but the displaced city has collapsed structures, injured residents, and immediate relief needs. Arlo cannot return it with his ordinary resources. Closetland remains on friendly terms with the dragon rulers and hosts their ambassadorial project, while Littan cooperation has deepened through the expedition and the Empire's acceptance of Grotto's identity. The stronger corrupting beast in the forest center remains at large. The six monoliths, the system orphan they feed, the recurring avatar cycle, Etja's growing internal emptiness, and the final consequences of Hysteria's apparent death also remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: An outside influence has distorted Fortune's Folly's priorities. The party traces it to Hysteria, uses Etja's retained fragment to empower Arlo's Soul Sight, removes the alterations with Varrin's soul-cutting and Nuralie's poison, and destroys the fragment. Avarice then apparently kills the imprisoned Hysteria. After individual ruler trials, the party meets ancient dragon rulers who explain that avatar disasters recur and that six monoliths are feeding a system orphan. Closetland gains friendly relations and a dragon ambassador. Fortune's Folly joins a Littan forest expedition, where an unknown force drives mana monsters against a border city. The attackers are controlled by the Hierophant, whose body conceals a surviving staff entity. A soul rite gives Arlo enough temporary blessed power for him and Etja to move the whole city into Closetland. Arlo and the Littan major destroy the staff, leaving the city alive but damaged, displaced, and in urgent need of aid.

recaps.text: Previously: Arlo Xor'Drel travels with Varrin, Xim, Etja, and Nuralie as Fortune's Folly. Grotto is Arlo's soul-linked Delve partner, and together they oversee the developing refuge of Closetland. The party has already become entangled with avatars and other higher powers, including Avarice, Fortune, and the hostile Orexis. Those conflicts have left them wary of divine bargains, spiritual coercion, and the System's larger purposes. Their unusual advancement and access to a Pocket Delve also make them important to neighboring powers. Arlo's dimensional abilities give the group exceptional mobility. Varrin supplies frontline force, Xim combines divine combat with healing, Etja controls and reshapes magic, and Nuralie joins alchemy and archery with reconnaissance. Grotto supports both the group and Closetland through his Delve abilities. Fortune's Folly begins this volume with a capable, closely linked team, a growing territory to protect, and unresolved avatar threats that make further advancement and outside alliances increasingly important.

Avarice supplies essences for Closetland and warns that most of Fortune's Folly is under an outside influence that changes decisions while preventing the affected members from retaining an explanation. Grotto is unaffected, and Etja resists enough of the effect to receive veto power over the party's dealings. The group cautiously accepts the prospect of a joint Littan dungeon expedition, then travels north to advance. In a buried expansion Delve, the party faces ancient undead legions, steals prismatite and weapons from an armory, and frees a spectral guardian from its bindings. The Delve Core retaliates by sending them into a killbox filled with undead forces and soul-collecting machinery. Fortune's Folly destroys the first commander and damages the collectors, but the resulting containment failure reveals a masked Grade 51 elder lich. The depleted party now faces an opponent far beyond the Delve's earlier commanders, while the hidden influence on its own members remains unresolved.

The Elder Lich general withdraws after explaining that his army pursues avatars rather than territory and that it condemns involuntary control. Fortune's Folly defeats the hostile Delve Core, takes it into custody as Throne, and considers Heavenly Gates, a Dread Star evolution that would make Arlo's travel magic deific. The party's concern about its compromised reasoning grows. Arlo and Etja map abnormal threads within their companions' souls and use Varrin's unaffected ancestral clone as a baseline. Their working theory is that the influence changes emotional importance rather than memories. Nuralie adapts earlier anti-Orexis work into a focused soul poison, while Etja's retained Hysteria fragment offers the power needed to reveal the corruption. The party prepares toxin-bearing spiritual scalpels and a ritual intended to keep divine energy from killing Arlo. He accepts Heavenly Gates, confirms that its travel effects operate through his soul, and commits to being the first subject of the dangerous procedure.

Fortune's Folly conducts its soul operation inside the Pocket Delve. Xim creates a shared ritual space, Etja contains Hysteria's fragment, Arlo uses its essence to sharpen Soul Sight, Varrin cuts out the altered portions, and Nuralie's poison destroys them. When the fragment tries to restore the corruption through a concealed channel, the party forces it into the open and destroys its identity. The members separate to recover, with Arlo suffering the deepest soul damage. Elsewhere, Avarice tests the imprisoned Hysteria after the avatar's wound changes. Her soul-draining golem reduces Hysteria's manifested soul to nothing, and the System later credits Fortune's Folly with contributing to the death. Arlo's recovery confirms that Hysteria's influence has left his soul, although its earlier goals remain only partly understood. The party receives rare rewards and postpones further travel long enough to investigate whether its captive beastmaster still carries the same manipulation.

Arlo examines the captive beastmaster with her consent and finds that Hysteria exploited existing trauma, strengthening anger and misplaced trust without creating the original wounds. He maps and then removes the remaining influence at her request. Accepting that her earlier actions were conditioned, he offers a path toward freedom, citizenship, or work in Closetland after recovery. The party also studies captured ancient rifles and armor, deciding against creating intelligent weapons without meaningful freedom while preparing practical equipment upgrades. Etja receives prismatite-infused armor and develops a party-wide use of Haste. Fortune's Folly then resumes its northern journey and reaches a mountain protected by an extraordinarily powerful gatekeeper. Avarice's token grants entry, but each member must face an individual test. The entrance separates the party, and Arlo finds himself trapped in a shifting Dimensional Dungeon beyond the reach of normal party links.

The separated party members undertake ruler trials. Arlo bypasses spatial traps with deific teleportation and draws the attention of a younger dimensional ruler and an older ruler. Etja turns a predatory mass of pure mana against itself by opening the internal emptiness within her, though that emptiness is becoming harder to contain. Varrin duels a far stronger elemental remembrance, wins the physical trial, receives equipment for controlling his rage, and improves his understanding of physical magic. Nuralie enters a spiritually divided forest where undead hunters feed living prey to a vast soul-devouring creature. She builds a soulless stealth construct, attacks through it with holy soul-poisoned arrows, and escapes the target's destructive counterattack. The poison kills both the creature and most of its defenders, although the construct is lost. Etja has reversed the immediate mana threat, Varrin has won his trial, Nuralie has eliminated her target, and Arlo continues down an extremely long corridor.

Arlo trains until his dimensional skill reaches a new threshold, then duels the ruler's daughter under rules that allow equipment and ordinary abilities but forbid higher-power intervention. He uses Closetland portals, redirected attacks, and a ring of dimensional beams to overcome her defenses. She transforms into a silver dragon, revealing the nature she had concealed, but the older ruler declares her defeated and ends the contest. The party reunites after its separate trials, except for Xim. Her test is administered by a crystalline divine figure who identifies her as a seeker pursuing all seven organ-based revelations toward becoming her deity's vessel. Xim accepts an overwhelming grant of divine knowledge and survives. In the resulting vision she sees six monoliths receiving power through a tear in the heavens, with two already active. She concludes that the coming catastrophe is unnatural and that she is obligated to oppose it.

Fortune's Folly receives an audience with five dragon rulers and presents its evidence concerning Hysteria. The Scarlet ruler recounts repeated avatar wars, failed prisons, and earlier catastrophes that destroyed advanced civilizations. The dragons once worked with Avarice and Fortune to build an avatar cage, but even that effort failed to end the cycle. Silver's attempt to flee the planet also failed, leading the rulers to believe the System prevented escape. Violet warns privately that killing current avatars cannot solve a threat the System can recreate. Gold explains that the six monoliths nourish the first and greatest system orphan, with two active and another activation near. The rulers do not promise military support, but Silver appoints the dragon princess as ambassador to Closetland. Formal friendly relations follow, including an embassy plan and controlled access through Arlo's checkpoint. After months of training and administration, Closetland has recognition and new growth plans, but no binding alliance.

Heavenly Gates changes Arlo's Delve assignments into missions to repair or shut down dangerous malfunctions. Fortune's Folly completes three such interventions, reaches level 16, and prepares for the delayed Littan expedition. Arlo strengthens his armor, regeneration, and healing, while the party questions the Dread Star about its motives. Its answers suggest that it needed a free-willed mortal channel after serious violations, but the party's theory that avatars are remnants cast off by flawed Ascension remains an interpretation rather than settled truth. At the Littan fortress, the major reports that the conflict with Eshendur has formally ended through shared institutions and improved trade. Fortune's Folly will serve as foreign consultants outside the Imperial command chain but still subject to Imperial law. The party meets the level-16 Littan captain who leads the accompanying five-person team and prepares to depart for the vast, only partly mapped forest dungeon.

Imperial analysts consider it plausible, but unconfirmed, that one of the six monoliths lies within the forest. Fortune's Folly proceeds with its assigned exploration mission rather than treating the journey as a monolith search. During the flight, the party meets the Littan captain's dimensional mage, frontline defender, and identical twins with complementary martial and stealth abilities. The Littan mage studies Arlo's Pocket Delve and deduces that Grotto is the surviving Core of the destroyed creation Delve. Arlo confirms the relationship, and the Littan officers accept the disclosure without conflict. An enormous swarm of nearly invisible silica swifts then attacks the transport. After the Littan team breaks much of the flock, unexplained pressure pulses drive both birds and the hammerhead toward a border city. The transport falls when the animal breaks free, but Varrin replaces it in flight and carries the cabin onward. Communication with the city fails, so both parties prepare for a high-speed emergency approach.

The expedition finds a Littan border city overwhelmed by avian mana monsters and missing its strongest defenders. The swarm is being empowered by a huge Hierophant whose living canopy upgrades birds. Fortune's Folly agrees to attack the alpha while the Littan team handles its elite guards, and the dragon princess supplies fifty juvenile red dragons to defend the airspace. The combined force turns its aircraft into a trapped, poisoned projectile and strikes the creature at extreme speed, but the opening blow removes only a small portion of its health. The Hierophant reaches Grade 34, heals through stolen humanoid heads, spreads a toxic aura, and bombards Arlo and the city with mystical attacks. The party and dragons gradually prevent replacement heads from reaching it. A coordinated anti-magic opening lets Arlo and Etja blast the body into the forest and destroy it. The apparent victory fails when the staff detaches from the corpse, survives, and reveals itself as the true active entity preparing a larger attack.

The surviving staff offers to spare the city only if its people are surrendered as food and a nest. It also claims that a stronger corrupting beast drove it from the forest center. The defenders reject the demand. The Littan major, captain, frontline fighter, dimensional mage, and Xim conduct a soul-linked rite using the battlefield dead, granting Arlo an immense temporary reserve of blessed power. When the staff fires catastrophic beams, the frontline fighter partly deflects one, but the city cannot survive a continuing exchange. The major and captain secure mass consent, allowing Arlo and Etja to expand Shortcut and Siphon across the entire settlement. They teleport the city and its inhabitants into Closetland before the next beam arrives. Arlo and the major then attack the staff directly, interrupt its final cleansing attempt, and destroy it. The Hierophant is dead, but the displaced city has structural damage and injured residents, and Arlo lacks the extraordinary power needed to return it. Relief and restoration begin under the continuing threats of the forest beast, the monoliths, and the wider avatar cycle.

characters.description: A newly graduated immaterial guide who reaches Bandfast with her keystone intact but her supporting inscriptions lost. Her precise gravity workings are expressed through her hands, and heavy academy and family debts leave her urgently seeking paid work.
characters.name: Tala

characters.description: A material creator at Bandfast's teleportation tower. Phoen helps confirm that Tala's keystone still functions, then explains how its survival complicates her choice between accepting mageling pay and seeking employment at a mage's rate.
characters.name: Phoen

characters.description: An unidentified humanoid arcane that holds Tala's attention through an apparent conceptual allure and then causes her to doubt the encounter. Tala's keystone confirms that the manipulation occurred, but the figure's identity and purpose remain unknown.
characters.name: Humanoid arcane

characters.description: A senior former checker who recruits for the Caravaner's Guild. Lyn detects Tala's intact keystone, negotiates her long-term caravan contract, and begins arranging the practical support needed for her first assignment.
characters.name: Lyn

characters.description: A master inscriber who finds that Tala's sophisticated existing design is poorly matched to her body and needs. Holly proposes an expensive, staged replacement intended to make Tala's passive inscriptions more durable and effective.
characters.name: Holly

characters.description: A Bandfast-raised caravan guard assigned to Tala's coming journey. Though initially cautious around her because she is a mage, Ashin serves as her local guide and helps her obtain the basic equipment needed for the trip.
characters.name: Ashin

characters.description: A Wainwright arbiter, Archon, and expert in dimensional cargo workings. Himmal tests Tala's capacity, teaches her to empower spell forms through a clear mental model, and offers to sponsor her for Archon status when she is ready.
characters.name: Himmal

characters.description: A material creator specializing in kinetic energy who meets Tala in the Guild mage lounge. Her strange appearance under Mage Sight unsettles him, but his curiosity leads him to share a meal and introduce her to other caravan mages.
characters.name: Cran

characters.description: A material guide specializing in ice and lightning who will help defend the Alefast caravan. Trent is Renix's master, and his first examination of Tala under Mage Sight leaves him alarmed by her unusual magical defenses.
characters.name: Trent

characters.description: Trent's mageling, a material creator who works with ice and lightning. Renix is traveling as one of the Alefast caravan's defensive mages and reacts with fascination when allowed to examine Tala through Mage Sight.
characters.name: Renix

characters.description: An earthworking material guide assigned to defend the Alefast caravan. Atrexia can manipulate rock, soil, and related substances, and she immediately investigates Tala's unusual presence under Mage Sight.
characters.name: Atrexia

characters.description: The driver of the lead dimensional cargo wagon. Den is uneasy about Tala choosing to walk beside the caravan, but he accommodates her by storing her pack, explaining her options, and allowing her to use the wagon's roof seat.
characters.name: Den

characters.description: The guard commander responsible for the Alefast caravan. Divner oversees the armed force protecting the wagons, confirms that Tala's dimensional cargo slots are ready, and gives the order to depart Bandfast.
characters.name: Divner

characters.description: A caravan guard who takes part in protecting the convoy in the wilds. After an Arcanous bird is killed, Adam gives Tala permission to claim the unassigned remains for her experiments and possible future use.
characters.name: Adam

characters.description: The caravan's head chef and a keeper of its hidden Arcanous-meat practice. Brand attacks Tala when she discovers the secret, then explains that selected workers have eaten such meat for decades in hopes of gaining strength and improved healing.
characters.name: Brand

characters.description: An intelligent magical predator capable of precise teleportation. It ambushes Tala beside the caravan, breaks both bones in her left forearm, and escapes both her continuing gravity restraint and Renix's attempted lightning strike.
characters.name: Dimensional terror bird

characters.description: A caravan passenger who commissions Tala to obtain one thunderbolt horn for a spouse's treatment and promises five gold ounces in payment.
characters.name: Thunderbolt-horn passenger

characters.description: A massive creature hunted for a commissioned horn. Tala finds one alone and attacks it with a partly exposed ending-tree stick, damaging its skull. The wounded creature answers with an immense lightning strike.
characters.name: Thunderbolt

characters.description: A powerful regional creature whose horns provide protection and whose antlers produce lightning. It confronts the caravan before the mountain pass, joining battle with the defensive mages and seriously injuring Renix.
characters.name: Midnight Fox

characters.description: An Alefast merchant connected to the Order of the Harvest through Brand. Artia deals in magical objects and offers Tala equipment and dimensional storage in exchange for useful harvests from Arcanous Beasts.
characters.name: Artia

characters.description: The head of Alefast's local Archon Council. Grediv examines Tala's blood-made drops, confirms that they are weak Archon Stars, and recognizes both her unusual magical defenses and her ability to perceive within her own body.
characters.name: Grediv

recaps.ending: Tala reaches Alefast with the outward caravan, completes delivery of the dimensional cargo slots, and receives her pay. Trent, Atrexia, and the recovering Renix lodge at the Wandering Magician, where Tala also takes a room. Adam plans to continue her combat training on the return journey, while Brand's Order of the Harvest remains a secret alliance. The passenger has received one thunderbolt horn, but the spouse's treatment has no recorded outcome. Artia trades Tala an adaptive dimensional pouch and an artifact knife for preserved harvests, and Tala plans to consult Artia's husband about storage theory. Grediv confirms that Tala's merged blood drop contains genuine Archon Stars, but they are far too weak for evaluation. He offers introductory material, warns her away from time magic, and advises secrecy until she can create a star about forty times stronger. Tala remains bound to the Guild, owes Holly eight gold ounces, and still needs deeper and left-hand inscription work. She begins testing the pouch as it forms a usable interior and asks for power. The intelligent terror bird remains alive and nearby, with its purpose unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Newly graduated and heavily indebted, Tala reaches Bandfast with most of her inscriptions lost. She joins the Caravaner's Guild, receives a powerful staged redesign from Holly, and becomes cargo mage for a caravan to Alefast. In the wilds she joins Brand's covert Order of the Harvest, gathers dangerous magical materials, survives attacks, and attracts the attention of an intelligent teleporting terror bird. Her experiments produce weak blood Archon Stars, while Adam begins teaching her combat. Tala kills a thunderbolt and saves the caravan from a Midnight Fox, though Renix is badly hurt. In Alefast she completes her cargo assignment, trades preserved harvests to Artia for an artifact pouch and knife, and meets Grediv. He confirms her path toward becoming an Archon but warns that her star must become about forty times stronger before evaluation. Tala ends the book studying her adaptive pouch while the terror bird remains nearby.

recaps.text: Tala arrives in Bandfast by teleportation with her keystone intact but her supporting inscriptions erased. Burdened by academy and inherited family debt, she seeks work through the Caravaner's Guild. Recruiter Lyn discovers that Tala already qualifies as a mage and signs her to a five-year or thirty-trip contract as a specialist in dimensional cargo wagons. Lyn also introduces her to Holly, a master inscriber who finds serious flaws in Tala's old design. Tala agrees to a costly staged reconstruction, paying part immediately and promising the remainder after two jobs. Ashin, a guard on her first planned caravan, helps her buy supplies and prepare iron salve, which she uses to shield herself from direct magic. Holly discovers that Tala has exceptionally high power density but accumulates power slowly. A complete redesign would endanger her, so Holly installs a new continuous passive system while postponing the deeper work and Tala's left hand. When the inscriptions activate, Tala wakes with overwhelming sensory and physical enhancement and repeatedly injures herself while relearning basic movement. With Holly and Lyn's help she regains enough control to walk, but four days have passed and her first departure is close.

Holly activates Tala's unusually detailed Mage Sight, which can focus through walls and detect distant magic. Tala then renews her iron coating, leaving most of her magical presence hidden while her eyes remain conspicuous to other mages. At the Wainwright yard she proves able to power increasingly large dimensional cargo slots. The hardest test drains her into unconsciousness, but Himmal teaches her to replace brute force with a precise mental model, greatly improving her efficiency. He also reveals himself as an Archon and offers future sponsorship. In the Guild lounge Tala meets Cran, then the defensive mages Trent and Renix, all of whom react strongly to her strange appearance under Mage Sight. Before leaving Bandfast, five robbers corner her. Tala restrains all of them with altered gravity, sends one for the guards, and earns a reward without killing anyone. She uses the money to secure lodging with Lyn. At dawn she joins an eight-wagon caravan bound for Alefast. Den takes charge of her pack, Divner commands the guards, and earthworking mage Atrexia joins Trent, Renix, and Tala in the caravan's magical contingent. Tala confirms that her unfinished left hand still cannot power the cargo workings, then the convoy departs.

The caravan leaves Bandfast's defenses and enters the wilds, where abundant magic and dangerous creatures force constant vigilance. Tala discovers that her new mind gives her near-perfect recall, and Renix lends her inscription theory. Atrexia drives off a charging thundercattle bull, while guards kill a giant Arcanous bird that dives at Tala. She claims its talons and bones and seals them with iron salve. That night Tala learns that head chef Brand has secretly served the bird's meat. He attempts to silence her, but her defensive inscriptions stop his knife. Brand then explains that selected caravan workers have eaten Arcanous meat for decades despite a prohibition imposed by mages. Tala agrees to investigate the practice and later watches its magic move through Trent and Atrexia without immediate harm. A carnivorous plant attacks Tala at dawn, but her defenses hold until she destroys its core with a borrowed sword. Brand formally admits her to the Order of the Harvest, providing its notebook and identifying token. After further encounters with magical wildlife, Tala collects a branch and berries from an ending tree whose touch dissolves living matter. Trent warns that the sample is an easily concealed killing tool. Tala says she wants to study its opposition to her defenses and accepts his and Renix's informal guidance before attempting anything major.

Brand explains that an intact ending berry can grant temporary resistance to ordinary physical harm, while damage to its seed may kill the consumer. Tala carefully processes two seeds and later eats a berry after an intelligent terror bird teleports beside her, breaks her arm, and escapes her gravity restraint. Atrexia heals the injury. The bird returns peacefully on another night and accepts jerky, leaving its motives uncertain. Meanwhile, Tala refines her cargo-working technique and begins experimenting with power carried in her own blood. The drops merge into a stable spinning sphere linked to her perception. Trent recognizes it as an apparent Archon Star, and Atrexia confirms the resemblance, though it contains at least fifty times less power than expected. Tala can create and combine these weak stars quickly, but doing so leaves her exhausted and ravenous. A passenger offers five gold ounces for a thunderbolt horn needed for a spouse's treatment. Tala finds a thunderbolt and attacks it with her ending-tree branch. The wounded beast unleashes lightning that strips away much of her salve and burns her, yet her defenses regenerate the damage. Its own attack destroys its exposed brain. The caravan harvests the carcass, Tala secures both horns, and the terror bird feeds at the site without attacking anyone.

Tala delivers one thunderbolt horn to the passenger and accepts payment, offering the second if the planned healing construct requires it. Brand promises her a share of the preserved meat and an introduction to an Alefast dimensional-storage seller. Renix confides that he wants independence but feels unready to leave Trent's service, and Tala urges him to define the habits and sacrifices his desired future requires. The terror bird appears in a smaller form, accepts food, doubles in size through dimensional magic, and vanishes, proving that ordinary restraint cannot hold it. Tala asks Adam for combat instruction. He begins with balance, breathing, posture, observation, and independent judgment rather than weapons. Her concurrent experiments produce another weak Archon Star and reveal magic moving with the air in her lungs. As the caravan approaches a dangerous mountain pass, a Midnight Fox attacks. Its lightning injures Renix, but Tala tears away its antlers with escalating gravity, causing the stored lightning to destroy its body. Permanent death is uncertain. Renix survives with numerous broken bones and a concussion. Trent reassures Tala that her intervention saved the caravan and defines her best combat role as a protected single-target striker. The convoy clears the pass and nears the waning city of Alefast, while signs show that the terror bird is still following.

Alefast's gate mages inspect the caravan because a magical entity reportedly impersonated an entire caravan. Tala's iron-based defenses cause a dispute, but the gate commander admits the wagons. Tala completes her cargo assignment, receives payment, and sends messages to Holly and the Wainwrights through Lyn. Trent directs her to the Wandering Magician, where he, Atrexia, and the recovering Renix are staying. Brand introduces Tala to Artia, an Order-connected dealer in magical items. Tala trades preserved parts from Arcanous Beasts and her spare thunderbolt horn for an artifact knife and a dimensional belt pouch that appears to offer an additional spatial defense. At the inn, Grediv, head of the local Archon Council, examines Tala's blood creations. Two drops merge before him, and he confirms that they contain genuine but very weak Archon Stars. Grediv warns that Tala is operating far beyond her limited training. He offers introductory study material, forbids her from investigating time magic before becoming an Archon, and explains that a star is a point through which the soul learns to influence external magic. He advises Tala to delay evaluation until she can make one about forty times stronger. Tala settles into the inn, restores her iron salve, and enters the artifact pouch. It forms a usable interior around her needs and appears to request magical power. She remains indebted, incompletely inscribed, and followed by the unresolved terror bird, but now has a concrete path toward Archon status.

characters.description: An orphan boy of about thirteen kept as a ward of Castle Crydee's kitchen, on the Far Coast of the Kingdom of the Isles. He gathers shellfish, runs errands, and is due to be offered to the castle's craftmasters on Choosing Day along with the other boys of his year. Small for his age and quicker with his wits than with his hands, he privately doubts any master will want him, and he is quietly infatuated with the Duke's daughter, a girl far above anything an orphan could reasonably hope for.
characters.name: Pug

characters.description: Pug's closest friend, son of Castle Crydee's cook and his wife, a head taller and broader than Pug and a natural athlete. He has wanted a soldier's life for as long as he can remember and talks openly of serving in the Duke's guard. He treats Pug as a brother rather than a competitor, and the two have grown up together in the keep.
characters.name: Tomas

characters.description: The Duke of Crydee's magician: a stout, bearded man rarely seen without his pipe, who keeps a tower room crowded with books, scrolls and instruments. Magic is a suspect trade in the Kingdom and its practitioners are commoners of uncertain standing, so he holds his place at court on the Duke's favour and his own good sense. On Choosing Day he claims Pug as his apprentice when no craftmaster will take the boy.
characters.name: Kulgan

characters.description: The Duke of Crydee's daughter, close to Pug in age, dark-haired and accustomed to being obeyed. She is sharp-tongued, headstrong, and impatient with the narrow life expected of a nobleman's daughter on the Far Coast, and she is a good deal more aware of Pug than he dares to imagine.
characters.name: Princess Carline

characters.description: Borric conDoin, Duke of Crydee and Warden of the West, cousin to the King and one of the great lords of the Kingdom of the Isles. A widower who rules the Far Coast from his castle with a soldier's directness, he presides over the Choosing himself and takes a personal interest in the boys of his household.
characters.name: Duke Borric

characters.description: The Duke's elder son and heir to Crydee, fair-haired and open-tempered, easy with the castle's servants and popular with the garrison. He is the more diplomatic of the two brothers and the one expected to hold the duchy after his father.
characters.name: Lyam conDoin

characters.description: The Duke's younger son, dark, lean and dry-humoured, with a swordsman's quickness and a habit of saying exactly what he thinks. He is the sharper and less trusting of the two brothers, and he takes soldiering and the defence of the Far Coast very seriously.
characters.name: Arutha conDoin

characters.description: An elderly priest of Astalon attached to the Duke's household, who has taught the castle's children their letters and numbers for two generations. Dry, exacting and formidably learned, with a priest's own quiet arts, he takes a share in Pug's schooling alongside Kulgan.
characters.name: Father Tully

characters.description: Kulgan's franklin and household man, a big, weather-beaten former soldier from the mountains who keeps the magician's rooms, does the cooking, and handles anything that calls for a strong arm or a level head. He is taciturn but reliable, and he accepts Pug's arrival without comment.
characters.name: Meecham

characters.description: A firedrake, a small distant cousin of the true dragons, who has attached himself to Kulgan's tower for the hearth and the food. He is intelligent, wilful, and comes and goes entirely as he pleases, and he takes an immediate liking to the new apprentice.
characters.name: Fantus

characters.description: A sergeant of the Crydee garrison, born in the Empire of Great Kesh to the south, a broad and dark-skinned soldier of long service. Steady, good-humoured and entirely competent, he is trusted by the Duke and by both of the Duke's sons.
characters.name: Gardan

characters.description: A squire of the Duke's court, son of the Baron of Tulan, a little older than Pug. Charming, quick with a joke and quicker to take offence, he has ambitions regarding the Duke's daughter and does not welcome the sudden elevation of a kitchen boy into the same circle.
characters.name: Roland

characters.description: Huntmaster of Crydee, a lean, self-contained man orphaned young, who spent part of his boyhood among the elves of Elvandar. He speaks their language, is welcome in their forest, and serves as the Duke's usual go-between with them. His skill with the longbow has no equal on the Far Coast, and he keeps his own counsel about almost everything else.
characters.name: Martin Longbow

characters.description: Queen of the elves of Elvandar, the great forest north of Crydee. Ageless in appearance, formal and careful in her dealings with humans, she rules with the counsel of her spellweavers and has kept her people apart from the Kingdom's affairs. Word of the strangers on the Far Coast is enough to bring her into council with the Duke.
characters.name: Queen Aglaranna

characters.description: Chieftain of the dwarven village of Caldara in the Grey Towers, a stocky, pipe-smoking veteran who leads his people's warriors. He knows the old mine workings beneath the mountains better than anyone alive and treats the danger there as a matter of routine.
characters.name: Dolgan

characters.description: A robed sorcerer encountered deep beneath the Grey Towers, keeping company with a dying dragon. He speaks as if he already knows who has come and why, sees that a gift is made, and offers no account of himself, his powers or his interest in the matter.
characters.name: Macros the Black

recaps.ending: The book closes in the middle of the Riftwar rather than at its resolution. The Tsurani hold the valley and the forests near the Grey Towers, and the Kingdom's western armies can contain them but not drive them out. Duke Borric has taken the field in the east with Lyam, leaving Arutha and Swordmaster Fannon to hold Crydee. Tomas, wearing the white and gold armour given to him beneath the mountains, fights alongside the elves of Elvandar and grows steadily less like the boy who left Crydee; the memories and appetites of its long-dead owner rise in him, and the elves fear what he is becoming as much as they value what he can do. Queen Aglaranna is caught between the two judgements. Pug, who has never managed ordinary magic, is caught up in fighting outside Crydee, uses what power he can reach, is overwhelmed and taken alive. Instead of being killed he is carried back through the rift to the invaders' own world as a prisoner, and Crydee counts him among the dead. Nothing is settled: the war has years left to run, the invaders' world is still unknown, and the sorcerer met beneath the mountains has explained nothing. The story continues directly in Magician: Master.
recaps.in_short: On the Far Coast of the Kingdom of the Isles, an orphan kitchen boy named Pug is chosen as apprentice to Kulgan, the Duke of Crydee's magician, while his friend Tomas is taken into the garrison. Pug proves unable to work magic by any method Kulgan knows, but he saves the Duke's daughter from trolls and is raised to squire. A wrecked ship brings the first evidence of strangers from another world, and Duke Borric carries the warning east to Krondor and to the unstable King in Rillanon. On the way his party is ambushed and driven into the abandoned dwarven mines, where Tomas is separated from the rest, meets a dying dragon and a sorcerer, and is given an ancient suit of white and gold armour that begins to change him. The invaders, the Tsurani, come through their rift in force and the Riftwar begins. The fighting grinds on for years, Tomas grows into something no longer entirely human, and Pug is captured outside Crydee and carried through the rift as a slave.

recaps.text: Pug is an orphan boy raised in the kitchens of Castle Crydee, on the Far Coast of the Kingdom of the Isles, where Duke Borric conDoin rules as Warden of the West. Caught out by a storm while gathering shellfish on the shore, he shelters through the worst of it and gets back to the keep in time for Choosing Day, the morning on which the castle's craftmasters take the year's boys as apprentices. His friend Tomas, the cook's son, is claimed by the swordmaster for the garrison. Pug is passed over by every master in turn and is left standing alone until Kulgan, the Duke's magician, takes him at the last moment. Magic is a suspect trade in the Kingdom and a magician's apprentice has no obvious future, but the choice lifts Pug out of the kitchen: he moves into the magician's tower, gains a place among the castle's people rather than its servants, and finds himself within sight of the Duke's household, including the Duke's daughter Carline.

Pug's lessons go badly. Kulgan's exercises simply will not work for him, and neither master nor apprentice can say why, though Kulgan and Father Tully both suspect the failure is not for want of ability. Life at the keep otherwise suits him: he inherits the company of Kulgan's firedrake Fantus, the friendship of Meecham, and lessons from Tully alongside the Duke's children. Out beyond the walls Pug comes on Princess Carline set upon by trolls and drives them off, and the Duke rewards him with the rank of squire and a small holding, which does not please the court's other squires, Roland in particular. Not long afterwards a vessel of unfamiliar make is wrecked on the coast. Its crew is gone, but a dying man is recovered whose dress, weapons and speech match nothing known on the Far Coast, and the objects found with him defeat Kulgan's understanding entirely. The Duke begins to treat the possibility of an unknown enemy seriously.

Kulgan and Tully reach an alarming conclusion: the strangers are not from anywhere in this world, but come through some kind of gateway from another. The elves of Elvandar are brought into council and confirm that something is moving in the forests. Part of Pug's difficulty is finally explained as well, since his talent appears not to answer to the methods Kulgan was taught and may belong to a different discipline altogether, one no human magician of the Kingdom practises. Duke Borric decides the warning has to be carried east in person, first to the Prince of Krondor and then, if necessary, to the King, and he sets out with Arutha, Kulgan, Pug, Tomas, Meecham, Gardan and Martin Longbow. Crossing toward the Grey Towers the party is ambushed in force by the dark elves of the northern forests, driven off the road, and forced to take shelter in the abandoned dwarven mines of Mac Mordain Cadal beneath the mountains.

The party is scattered in the dark of the mines. Tomas, separated and hunted, falls in with Dolgan, chieftain of the dwarves of the Grey Towers. Deeper still they come upon Rhuagh, an ancient dragon at the end of his life, attended by a sorcerer who seems to have been expecting them. Before the dragon dies, gifts are made, and Tomas receives a suit of white and gold armour older than any human kingdom. He puts it on. He and Dolgan work their way out through the mountains, while the Duke's party, believing Tomas lost, reaches the coast and takes ship, passing Sorcerer's Isle, a place sailors avoid, on the way to Krondor. Tomas begins to dream another man's memories, and finds himself growing stronger, quicker and stranger than he was.

At Krondor, Prince Erland hears the Duke out but can spare no army: the court is dominated by eastern rivals, chief among them Guy du Bas-Tyra, and the western warning is not believed. Borric and Pug travel on to the island capital of Rillanon to petition King Rodric himself, who proves unstable and difficult, veering between grand building schemes and suspicion, but who is finally persuaded to raise the Armies of the East. The warning comes too late to prevent what it predicted. The invaders, who call themselves Tsurani, come through their rift in strength, take the valley and the forests around the Grey Towers, and dig in. What follows is not a raid but a war of position for ground the enemy means to keep, and it settles into a grinding campaign through the forests of Crydee and Yabon.

The war becomes years of stalemate in the forests. Duke Borric takes the field in the east with Lyam, leaving Arutha to hold Crydee with Swordmaster Fannon, while Martin's trackers and the elves harry the invaders' flanks. Tomas, all but unrecognisable in the ancient armour, fights alongside the elves of Elvandar; Queen Aglaranna and her advisers watch his growing power with open unease, because his strength and his ruthlessness are no longer those of a boy from Crydee, and some of them argue that he should be killed. Pug continues to fail at ordinary magic while showing occasional flashes of something else entirely. When the Tsurani finally press Crydee itself, Pug is caught up in the fighting outside the walls, reaches for what power he can, and is overwhelmed and taken alive. Rather than killing him, the Tsurani carry him back through the rift to their own world as a prisoner. At home he is counted among the dead.

characters.description: Once an orphan boy of Crydee and a magician's apprentice who could not make his master's magic work, now four years a slave in a Tsurani labour camp in the swamps of Kelewan. He has learned the language and something of the Empire that holds him, keeps his head down, and has largely given up expecting to see his own world again. He is still the same stubborn, observant boy underneath, and still carries a talent nobody, himself included, has been able to explain.
characters.name: Pug

characters.description: A travelling singer from Tyr-Sog in the Kingdom's north, captured by the Tsurani and sent to the swamp camp. Glib, adaptable and endlessly talkative, he has an ear for languages and an ambition to be a great minstrel that survives even slavery. He attaches himself to Pug, and the two keep each other alive.
characters.name: Laurie

characters.description: A slave on the Shinzawai estate, taken as a girl when the Empire subdued the Thuril highlands. Proud, sharp-tempered and unbroken by her position, she works in the household and makes no secret of what she thinks of the people who own her. She and Pug find an understanding.
characters.name: Katala

characters.description: Lord of the Shinzawai, head of one of the Empire's great houses and a careful player of the Game of the Council, the endless contest of position among Tsurani nobles. He has fought in the war on the barbarian world and has come to conclusions about it that he cannot state openly.
characters.name: Kamatsu of the Shinzawai

characters.description: Elder son of the Lord of the Shinzawai and an officer of the Empire's forces in the war beyond the rift. Disciplined and formal in the Tsurani manner, he is set to learn the Kingdom's language from his father's newly bought slaves, for a purpose the household will not discuss.
characters.name: Kasumi of the Shinzawai

characters.description: Younger son of the Lord of the Shinzawai, quieter and more thoughtful than his brother, and more willing to deal with a slave as a person. He is being raised to the same duties and the same discretion as the rest of the household.
characters.name: Hokanu of the Shinzawai

characters.description: The boy from Crydee's kitchens who was given a suit of ancient white and gold armour beneath the Grey Towers. He now fights alongside the elves of Elvandar and is more than a match for anything the Tsurani send against him, but the armour has brought with it the memories, the power and the temper of Ashen-Shugar, one of the Valheru who ruled Midkemia before men existed. Less of Tomas is left with every battle, and the elves are divided over whether he is their protector or their next disaster.
characters.name: Tomas

characters.description: Queen of the elves of Elvandar, ruler of the forest and its spellweavers. She is drawn to the transformed human warrior who has come to her forest and afraid of him at the same time, and she must weigh her council's demand that he be destroyed against what his strength is worth to her people in a war they cannot win alone.
characters.name: Queen Aglaranna

characters.description: The Duke of Crydee's younger son, dark and dry-humoured, left holding the Far Coast while his father and brother fight in the east. With Crydee starved of reinforcements he takes ship for Krondor to argue the west's case in person, and finds the city very different from the one his family remembers.
characters.name: Arutha conDoin

characters.description: A boy thief of Krondor, a member of the Mockers, the city's thieves' guild, and by his own account the best of them. Cocky, fast, and far better informed about Krondor than anyone in the palace, he attaches himself to a visiting nobleman out of curiosity and calculation, and turns out to be worth a great deal more than his years suggest.
characters.name: Jimmy the Hand

characters.description: Daughter of the ailing Prince of Krondor and heir to the Western Realm, a young woman kept close by the man now governing the city in the King's name. Slight, quiet and a good deal tougher than she looks, she has been waiting for a chance to get out.
characters.name: Princess Anita

characters.description: Duke of Bas-Tyra, the most powerful lord of the Eastern Realm and the King's Viceroy in Krondor, where he rules in fact if not in name. Able, ruthless and entirely without sentiment, he is the conDoin family's long-standing rival and treats the west's demands for troops as a nuisance.
characters.name: Guy du Bas-Tyra

characters.description: A weather-beaten sea captain and former pirate working the Krondor waterfront, loud, profane in the way of sailors, and superbly competent with a ship. He has reasons of his own for wanting to be out of the city and throws in with the Prince's party.
characters.name: Amos Trask

characters.description: The Duke of Crydee's daughter, left at home while her family fights the war. Still headstrong, she has grown out of the girl she was, has mourned the apprentice believed killed at Crydee, and is looking for something to do beyond waiting on other people's news.
characters.name: Princess Carline

characters.description: A Great One of the Tsurani Assembly of Magicians: stout, comfortable, fond of his food and a great deal shrewder than he lets himself appear. The Great Ones stand outside Tsuranuanni's law and above its lords, and he has spent a long career understanding exactly what that is worth. He takes an interest in the Assembly's most unusual new member.
characters.name: Hochopepa

characters.description: A sorcerer of great age and unclear allegiance who keeps an island the Kingdom's sailors will not approach. He appears where events are turning, gives advice without explaining his reasons, and appears to know a great deal more about the war and its causes than anyone else alive.
characters.name: Macros the Black

recaps.ending: The Riftwar ends. The truce talks are broken by treachery and the fighting resolves into a final battle in the east, at Sethanon, where King Rodric is mortally wounded and names Lyam conDoin his heir before he dies. Pug, no longer using his Tsurani name, and Tomas take a hand in the battle, and the sorcerer Macros closes the rift between the worlds at the apparent cost of his own life, stranding the Tsurani army on Midkemia for good. Lyam is crowned in Rillanon. There it emerges that Martin Longbow, huntmaster of Crydee, is Duke Borric's natural son and therefore Lyam's elder half-brother with a claim on the crown; Martin renounces it publicly and the succession holds. Arutha becomes Prince of Krondor and is betrothed to Anita; Martin is confirmed Duke of Crydee; Carline and Laurie find each other; Kasumi's stranded Tsurani soldiers swear to the Kingdom and are settled at LaMut under his command. Pug and Katala remain on Midkemia to build a life and, in time, a place where magic can be studied openly. Tomas, now at peace with the Valheru memories he carries, shares the rule of Elvandar with Aglaranna. What none of them can answer is what Macros knew, what the vision in Pug's final trial was warning of, or why the enemy that drove the Tsurani's ancestors across space should matter to Midkemia at all.
recaps.in_short: Carried through the rift at the end of Magician: Apprentice, Pug spends four years as a slave in the Tsurani swamps before he and a captured Kingdom singer, Laurie, are bought by the Shinzawai, a great house secretly working for peace. On their estate Pug meets and loves Katala, and the magical talent he could never use finally surfaces. The Assembly of Magicians claims him, trains him, and elevates him as the Great One Milamber. On Midkemia, Tomas is nearly consumed by the Dragon Lord whose armour he wears before he regains himself, and Prince Arutha rescues Princess Anita from Guy du Bas-Tyra's grip on Krondor with the help of a boy thief called Jimmy the Hand. Sickened by the slaughter staged at the Warlord's games, Milamber destroys the arena and flees Kelewan with Katala. Duke Borric dies of his wounds, the Tsurani peace attempt is betrayed, and the war ends in a battle at Sethanon where King Rodric is killed after naming Lyam his heir. Macros closes the rift and is lost, Lyam is crowned, and Martin Longbow is revealed as Borric's bastard son and renounces his claim.

recaps.text: Previously, in Magician: Apprentice: Pug, an orphan raised in Castle Crydee on the Far Coast of the Kingdom of the Isles, was chosen as apprentice to the Duke's magician Kulgan but could not work magic by any method his master knew. His friend Tomas joined the garrison. A wrecked ship revealed the existence of invaders from another world, and Duke Borric's journey east to warn the Prince of Krondor and the King came too late: the Tsurani opened a rift and seized the valley and forests near the Grey Towers, beginning a long war. On the way east the Duke's party was driven into the abandoned dwarven mines, where Tomas was separated from the rest and given a suit of ancient white and gold armour by a dying dragon, watched by a sorcerer who explained nothing. The armour began to fill Tomas with another being's memories and power, and he now fights alongside the elves of Elvandar, who fear what he is becoming. After years of stalemate Pug was caught in the fighting outside Crydee and carried back through the rift as a slave. At home he is believed dead. This book picks the story up four years later, with the war still running.

Pug has spent four years as a slave in a Tsurani swamp camp, cutting and hauling logs under brutal overseers. He has learned the language and something of the world called Kelewan and of Tsuranuanni, the rigid empire that rules it. A newly captured Kingdom man arrives, a travelling singer named Laurie, and the two become allies. Their situation changes when they are bought out of the camp and taken north to the estate of the Shinzawai, one of the Empire's great houses. Lord Kamatsu and his elder son Kasumi want one specific thing from them: someone to teach Kasumi to speak the King's Tongue like a native, for reasons nobody in the household will explain. Life on the estate is a different order of existence from the swamp. Pug is set to work in the gardens, where he meets Katala, a slave taken from the Thuril highlands, and for the first time since his capture he begins to build a life rather than simply survive.

On Midkemia, Tomas has all but disappeared into the armour he wears. The memories of Ashen-Shugar, one of the Valheru or Dragon Lords who ruled the world in an age before men, rise in him with every battle, and he becomes a warrior the Tsurani cannot stand against and a presence the elves of Elvandar cannot control. Queen Aglaranna is drawn to him and frightened of him at once, while her advisers argue that he must be destroyed before he turns on them. On Kelewan, Pug's life at the Shinzawai estate settles: he and Katala grow close, Laurie's lessons with Kasumi continue, and the household's purpose becomes a little clearer. Kamatsu belongs to a faction that wants the war ended, and their plan turns on getting a message to the Kingdom's King behind the Warlord's back. The family travels with their two Midkemian slaves in attendance, and Pug begins to show flashes of a power he cannot account for.

Pug's power breaks out where it cannot be concealed, and the Assembly of Magicians takes him: on Kelewan a man with the talent belongs to the Great Ones, who stand outside the law and above the great houses, and no lord's claim on a slave outweighs that. He is taken to the City of Magicians, freed of his slave status and put through a long and punishing training under masters including the stout, pragmatic Hochopepa. On Midkemia, Prince Arutha travels to Krondor to beg for reinforcements and finds the city in the hand of Guy du Bas-Tyra, the King's Viceroy and the conDoins' old rival, with Princess Anita, the heir of Krondor, effectively his prisoner. Arutha falls in with the Mockers, the city's thieves' guild, and with a young thief named Jimmy the Hand, and together they get Anita out of the palace and away.

Arutha, Anita and their companions escape Krondor by sea with the smuggler captain Amos Trask, survive a hard voyage, and reach Crydee, where Arutha and Anita's attachment deepens. On Kelewan, Pug completes the Assembly's training and passes its final trial, in which he is shown the history of the world and something of the ancient force that once drove the Tsurani's ancestors across space to reach it. He emerges as a Great One under the name Milamber, one of the most powerful magicians of the Empire, answerable to no lord and free to go where he pleases. He returns for Katala and marries her. In the north of Midkemia, Tomas is brought back from the edge by the intervention of the sorcerer Macros and by what remains of his own humanity, and finds a balance between the boy from Crydee and the Dragon Lord whose memories he carries. He and Aglaranna acknowledge each other openly.

Summoned with the other Great Ones to the Warlord's Imperial Games in the Holy City, Milamber watches Midkemian prisoners butchered for the crowd's entertainment and, in a rage he does not entirely control, tears the arena apart with storm and earthquake before walking out. By Tsurani standards the act is unforgivable, and it makes him an outlaw in all but name; he takes Katala and flees to Midkemia. The Assembly, humiliated, withdraws its support from the Warlord, and the political ground on Kelewan shifts far enough for the peace faction's plan to move. On Midkemia the war has ground on for years. Duke Borric is mortally wounded at the front and dies, and Lyam becomes Duke of Crydee. Kasumi crosses the rift under the Shinzawai plan carrying terms, and for the first time an end to the war looks possible.

The truce talks are broken by treachery: the Warlord's faction attacks under the flag of parley, and the fighting resolves into a final battle in the east, at Sethanon. King Rodric is mortally wounded there and names Lyam his heir before he dies. Pug and Tomas take a hand in the battle, and the sorcerer Macros closes the rift between the worlds at the apparent cost of his own life, cutting the Tsurani army on Midkemia off from home for good. The war ends. Lyam is crowned in Rillanon, where an old matter finally comes out: Martin Longbow, huntmaster of Crydee, is Borric's natural son and therefore Lyam's elder half-brother, with a claim on the crown. Martin renounces it publicly and the succession holds. Arutha becomes Prince of Krondor and is betrothed to Anita, Martin is confirmed Duke of Crydee, Carline and Laurie find each other, and Kasumi's stranded Tsurani soldiers swear to the Kingdom and are settled at LaMut. Pug and Katala remain on Midkemia, with the question of what Macros knew, and what his warning meant, still unanswered.

characters.description: An imaginative, college-educated young woman who works as a librarian in St. Paul and dreams of making ordinary places more beautiful and humane. Marriage brings her to Gopher Prairie, Minnesota, where her enthusiasm for reform meets habits and judgments she finds stifling.
characters.name: Carol Milford Kennicott

characters.description: A capable country doctor from Gopher Prairie who courts Carol in St. Paul. Proud of his town and his useful place within it, he is affectionate, practical, and largely puzzled by Carol's conviction that local life needs transformation.
characters.name: Dr. Will Kennicott

characters.description: A thoughtful lawyer in Gopher Prairie whose quiet manner and literary interests make him seem to Carol like a possible ally. He speaks of the town's numbing influence with insight, though he has made accommodation rather than rebellion his way of living there.
characters.name: Guy Pollock

characters.description: A teacher and leading member of Gopher Prairie's small intellectual circle. Energetic, civic-minded, and initially welcoming to Carol, she believes in gradual usefulness more than sweeping aesthetic reform.
characters.name: Vida Sherwin

characters.description: A young Swedish immigrant whom Carol employs as a maid. Warm, capable, and eager for friendship as well as work, she becomes one of the few people in town with whom Carol can relax without social calculation.
characters.name: Bea Sorenson

characters.description: A Swedish-American handyman and horse trader who lives at the edge of respectable Gopher Prairie society. Blunt and self-sufficient, he treats the town's class rules with open contempt and attracts Carol by refusing its pretenses.
characters.name: Miles Bjornstam

characters.description: A fashionable member of Gopher Prairie's leading social set and the wife of merchant Harry Haydock. She is friendly when Carol observes the town's conventions, but her confidence in local standards leaves little room for Carol's criticism.
characters.name: Juanita Haydock

characters.description: A prosperous Gopher Prairie merchant, booster, and member of Will's social circle. He regards commercial growth and club sociability as strong evidence that the town already offers everything reasonable people need.
characters.name: Harry Haydock

characters.description: A devout, censorious neighbor who treats private behavior as a matter for public supervision. Her son Cy's misbehavior rarely weakens her certainty about the faults of other townspeople.
characters.name: Mrs. Bogart

characters.description: Mrs. Bogart's unruly adolescent son, whose pranks and boastfulness contrast with his mother's rigid moral claims. He is one of the young people formed by the town's mixture of repression and tolerated cruelty.
characters.name: Cy Bogart

characters.description: A former Gopher Prairie boy who has become a nationally successful automobile executive. His return excites the town and presents Carol with an apparently sophisticated outsider who nevertheless celebrates the values she questions.
characters.name: Percy Bresnahan

characters.description: A young tailor of Swedish background who comes to work in Gopher Prairie. Sensitive, ambitious, and dissatisfied with the narrow future available to him, he shares Carol's hunger for beauty and a wider life.
characters.name: Erik Valborg

characters.description: A young teacher newly arrived in Gopher Prairie. Athletic, candid, and less guarded than the town expects a woman teacher to be, she becomes friendly with Carol and soon attracts close scrutiny from moralizing neighbors.
characters.name: Fern Mullins

characters.description: Carol and Will's young son. His needs bind Carol more closely to domestic life while also sharpening her concern about the kind of town and expectations that will shape him.
characters.name: Hugh Kennicott

recaps.ending: After living and working in Washington, D.C., Carol recognizes both the larger world's possibilities and the limits of escape. She returns voluntarily to Gopher Prairie with Hugh and resumes her marriage to Will. The town has changed only modestly, and Carol has not converted it to her early vision, but distance has made her less dependent on its approval. She accepts that reform is usually partial and slow without accepting the town's claim that nothing needs reform. Carol later gives birth to a daughter and insists that the child will not be taught to regard existing customs as sacred merely because they are familiar. Will remains practical, affectionate, and unconvinced by much of her language, yet their marriage now has more room for her dissent. The close offers neither triumph nor surrender: Carol continues imagining, questioning, and preparing to resist complacency from inside the community she once hoped simply to remake or flee.
recaps.in_short: Idealistic librarian Carol Milford marries country doctor Will Kennicott and moves to Gopher Prairie, Minnesota, expecting to beautify and reform the town. Its social clubs, commercial pride, gossip, and suspicion of difference defeat project after project, while Will remains loyal to local values. Carol finds partial companionship in Guy Pollock, Vida Sherwin, Bea Sorenson, and Miles Bjornstam, but the deaths of Bea and her child after an infection expose the community's harshness toward outsiders. Carol's attraction to the younger Erik Valborg becomes an emotional rebellion; he leaves before it becomes a new life. After further disillusionment, Carol takes her son Hugh to Washington, D.C., and works there for two years. She eventually returns to Will by choice. Gopher Prairie has not become her ideal, but it has not extinguished her refusal to question it. With a new daughter, Carol remains committed to keeping that spirit of independence alive.

recaps.text: Carol Milford, orphaned young and educated at Blodgett College, wants a life devoted to culture and social improvement. Work as a librarian in St. Paul does not satisfy her hope of transforming a community. She meets Will Kennicott, a competent doctor from the small Minnesota town of Gopher Prairie, and his confidence in the place persuades her that marriage could give her the field of action she wants. On arrival, Carol is shocked by the town's shabby main street, rigid social groupings, and aggressive pride in its own adequacy. Will's friends welcome her, but they treat her aesthetic criticism as affectation. Carol hires the Swedish immigrant Bea Sorenson and begins learning the town's network of clubs, businesses, churches, and gossip, still certain that energy and taste can remake it.

Carol tests her reforming ambitions through domestic entertaining, civic discussion, and proposals for a better library and public spaces. The town's leading women enjoy novelty when it remains decorative, but they resist any suggestion that Gopher Prairie is unjust or ugly. Carol finds sympathetic conversation with lawyer Guy Pollock, who understands the dulling force of the town but has ceased trying to escape it, and with teacher Vida Sherwin, who favors patient, practical work. She also befriends Miles Bjornstam, an independent laborer dismissed by respectable residents as an outsider. Will is generous and often amused by Carol's plans, yet his deep loyalty to local people makes her criticisms feel like attacks on his identity. Her first campaigns reveal that social opposition rarely appears as a direct argument; it works through delay, ridicule, and exclusion.

Carol organizes an amateur dramatic production, hoping collaborative art will awaken the town's imagination. Rehearsals collapse into vanity, carelessness, and demands for familiar entertainment, and the final performance falls far short of her vision. Other reform projects meet similar resistance. Motherhood gives Carol a new attachment to Gopher Prairie when her son Hugh is born, but it does not end her restlessness. Vida Sherwin chooses a more conventional path of useful local service, while Bea Sorenson and Miles Bjornstam marry despite the town's class prejudice. Their happiness briefly suggests a life outside respectable opinion. Carol remains divided between affection for individuals and anger at the collective habits that limit them, and she begins to understand that her own desire to direct people can also carry condescension.

The visit of successful businessman Percy Bresnahan gives Gopher Prairie a model of worldly achievement, but Carol discovers that his polish does not make him an ally against the town's complacency. Infection strikes the Bjornstam household, and both Bea and her young child die. The town's neglect and disdain leave Miles alone with losses that a more accepted family might have faced with greater support. Carol's faith in neighborly virtue weakens further. She meets Erik Valborg, a young tailor who longs for art, education, and escape from the future assigned to him. Their shared dissatisfaction creates an immediate intimacy. To Carol, Erik seems to restore the romantic and creative self that marriage and civic failure have compressed; to the town, their growing closeness becomes material for surveillance and gossip.

Carol and Erik's attachment approaches an affair, though much of its force lies in fantasy about leaving Gopher Prairie together. Will confronts the situation without the melodrama Carol half expects. Erik departs, and Carol remains, aware that passion alone did not provide a workable alternative life. The town soon turns on young teacher Fern Mullins after Cy Bogart engineers a compromising appearance; Mrs. Bogart and other guardians of morality force Fern out despite weak evidence against her. The episode confirms Carol's view that communal respectability protects insiders and sacrifices vulnerable outsiders. At the same time, Carol confronts strains within her marriage and the possibility that Will also seeks affection elsewhere. Neither rebellion nor accommodation has given her a durable sense of purpose.

Unable to continue on the same terms, Carol leaves Gopher Prairie with Hugh and moves to Washington, D.C., while remaining married to Will. She works in a wartime government office, earns her own money, meets people from different regions, and discovers that the wider world is neither a perfect escape nor merely a larger version of her town. After two years she returns to Will voluntarily, with a more realistic sense of what independence and reform require. Gopher Prairie has changed little, but Carol no longer expects one campaign or one romance to transform it. She later gives birth to a daughter and insists that the child should grow up free to question inherited customs. Carol has not defeated the town, yet she has preserved the part of herself that refuses to call its present arrangements inevitable. Her marriage and community remain imperfect settings in which that resistance will continue.

characters.description: An educated young librarian who longs to make ordinary places more beautiful, open-minded, and socially alive. After marrying a small-town doctor, she approaches Gopher Prairie with reforming enthusiasm and little understanding of how strongly its habits defend themselves.
characters.name: Carol Milford Kennicott

characters.description: A capable country doctor from Gopher Prairie who courts Carol with a practical promise of usefulness and community. Will is proud of his town, devoted to his work, and puzzled when Carol sees ugliness and complacency where he sees familiar people and solid achievement.
characters.name: Will Kennicott

characters.description: A clever, energetic Gopher Prairie teacher who initially appears more receptive than most townspeople to Carol's ideas. Vida combines genuine public spirit with a firm belief in working through the community's existing institutions.
characters.name: Vida Sherwin
